property_summary: For any new owner address, the admin (deployer) can always successfully set the owner to that address; the mutant restricts setOwner to the current owner instead, so calling as admin with a newOwner != owner fails or leaves owner unchanged, breaking the rule.
setOwner always returns true when it succeeds for any caller and any new owner; the mutant instead returns msg.sender == _owner, which is false whenever the caller sets a different owner.

property_summary: For any admissible new owner address, a successful call to setOwner always returns true; the mutant returns false when the new owner equals the current owner (an unchanged owner), breaking the rule.

For any caller, setOwner either (a) succeeds because the caller is admin, setting owner to the requested address, or (b) reverts with the owner state left completely unchanged; the mutant moves the onlyAdmin require after the effect, so a non-admin call can mutate state (exposed to reentrancy/transient reads) before reverting, breaking the atomic 'revert ⇒ no effect' rule for some fuzzed non-admin actor and target owner.

For every non-admin caller, setOwner must reject the call in the modifier BEFORE executing the body, so the failed call consumes less gas than a failed call that first performed a cold storage load+store of `owner`; the mutant executes the storage write before reverting, burning tens of thousands of extra gas even though the state is rolled back.

For every caller other than the admin, setOwner must revert before taking effect; the mutant's `return true` in the body skips the require placed after `_;`, so a non-admin call succeeds and changes `owner`, which the test detects by asserting the call is rejected.

For any non-admin caller, a successful setOwner must leave owner unchanged (the call must be rejected before effect); the mutant executes the write and returns before the require, so a non-admin call succeeds and permanently changes owner.

For any caller other than the deploy-time admin, setOwner must both revert (ok == false) and leave owner untouched; the mutant executes the body and `return true` skips the trailing require, so a non-admin call returns successfully with owner changed.
